Whats Really Going on at Fukushima?

An interesting article! Although the author has a bit of a "doomsday" tone, there are several good points brought up. I think its important to note first, however, that there is no credible evidence of "The China Syndrome", i.e. nuclear material melting through the core and containment vessels to seep into the earth (and consequently, the water table). In fact, a recent robotic excursion into the primary containment vessel showed very little damage, and temperature readouts indicated the cooling systems were functioning. I will admit that this was not in the number 4 reactor, which is the most damaged of the four units.

In any event, some good points the article brings up:

1) The long-term effects on the area are still unknown. This is true, because there hasn't really been an accident like this before (Chernobyl was significantly worse in terms of radiation release due to the zirconium fuel-cladding catching fire and throwing radioactive particles high into the atmosphere). However, early indications show that the Fukushima region has received less radiation than initially thought, and is actually within the "safe to inhabit" range.

2) Tens of thousands of people are still displaced from their homes. This is absolutely true. Although some people have returned to their homes, the government is reluctant to release the safety cordon from the region. This is both good and bad. In the event further disaster were to occur, those people are already evacuated, and loss of life can be minimized. The downside is that all of these people are effectively refugees, still living in tent cities with their lives in purgatory.

Unfortunately, many of the numbers in this article are greatly exaggerated (such as the 1 million person death toll from Chernobyl), so its hard to pick out fact from fancy.

Still, Thank you for your contribution!
